ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point E is on the diagonal BD of the rhombus ABCD, and DE = DA. Line AE is drawn. If $\angle CAE = 15^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle ABC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus, \\
it follows that AC $\perp$ BD, \\
since $\angle$CAE = 15$^\circ$, \\
thus, $\angle$AED = 90$^\circ$ - $\angle$EAC = 90$^\circ$ - 15$^\circ$ = 75$^\circ$, \\
since DE = DA, \\
it follows that $\angle$EAD = $\angle$AED = 75$^\circ$, \\
therefore, $\angle$ADB = $\angle$ABD = 30$^\circ$, \\
therefore, $\angle$ABC = 2$\angle$ADB = $2 \times 30^\circ$ = \boxed{60^\circ},

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, ABCD is a rhombus, placed in a rhombus/diamond shape; A is above, C is below, B is on the left, and D is on the right. Diagonal AC is drawn as a vertical line, and diagonal BD is drawn as a horizontal line. Point E is located on the horizontal diagonal BD, and is to the left of the intersection point of AC and BD; line segment AE has been drawn. Reasoning: Because ABCD is a rhombus, its two diagonals AC and BD are perpendicular to each other. E is on BD, so ED is perpendicular to AC. In triangle AED, it is known that ∠CAE = 15°, and AC and ED form 90°, so ∠AED = 90° - 15° = 75°. Also because the problem states that DE = DA, triangle ADE is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles are equal, that is, ∠EAD = ∠AED = 75°. Therefore ∠ADE = 180° - 75° - 75° = 30°. Since E is on BD, ∠ADE is ∠ADB, so ∠ADB = 30°. In the rhombus AD = AB, therefore triangle ABD is an isosceles triangle, and ∠ABD = ∠ADB = 30°. At the same time, the diagonal BD of the rhombus bisects vertex angle B, so ∠ABC = 2∠ABD = 2 × 30° = 60°.
